newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt prices continue rise, call unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt prices continue rise, call unchanged.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities continued to rise on Wednesday on buying interest fuelled by low call money rates, dealers said.
They said market attention was focussed largely in medium-term securities with maturities up to 2001 with prices moving up sharply in active trade.
"The bull-run is continuing," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But I think a correction is due sooner rather than later."
Prices of government securities have been rising steadily over the last two months on low call money rates and expectations of low interest rates.
The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) credit policy for first-half 1997/98 (April-March) announced steps to lower deposit rates. Several banks have cut prime lending rates.
The RBI also signalled a cut in long-term interest rates by reducing the cut-off yield on 10-year bonds to 13.05 percent from 13.65 percent at an auction on April 21.
Dealers said prices rose on Wednesday by as much as 2.0 rupees in some stocks.

The 13.65 percent 1999 traded on Wednesday at 106.60 rupees against its last traded 104.20, the zero-coupon 2000 rose to 70.70 rupees from 70.5, the 13.85 percent 2001 rose to 108 rupees from 107, dealers said.
Treasury bills were laso actively trade with April 1998 bills yileding 8.5 percent against last traded 8.7, they said.
Dealers said call money rates remained stuck in a narrow bank between 0.1 and 0.5 percent on Wednesday on good liquidity with banks.
Call money rates have been in the same range for the last two weeks as banks are flush with funds, dealers said.
A late-evening announcement on Wednesday of a private placement of bonds with the RBI could lead to a correction in prices of 10-year bonds, some dealers said.
The Finance Minstry announced the issue of 10-year 13.05 percent bonds for 50 billion rupees in a private placement deal with the RBI.
"The 10-year bond is trading in the secondary market at 12.60 percent," said a dealer. "This (the announcment) should lead to a slight correction in prices tomorrow in the 10-year bond."
The dealer said he expected selling pressure in the bond to push prices down on Thursday.
"People may switch to short-term paper now," said a dealer.
